title: Water Lilies
credit_line: Museum purchase, Mildred Anna Williams Collection
web_text: Dark blossoms and bright leaves drift among the reflected clouds on the water’s surface. No horizon is in sight. In the 1880s and 1890s, Monet developed a small natural pond on his property at Giverny into an extensive water garden inspired by Japanese ukiyo-e prints. This garden functioned as a kind of outdoor studio where he ultimately painted some two hundred fifty pictures, among them several of his most iconic works. This example likely dates to the mid-1910s but betrays no hint of the First World War raging not far from Giverny.
exhibition_history_text:
Washington, D.C., The National Gallery of Art, April–November 1971. Collection loan.

Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco (California Palace of the Legion of Honor), January 19– March 17, 1974; Santa Barbara Museum of Art, March 23–May 5, 1974; Fine Arts Gallery of San Diego, May 18–June 30, 1974. “Claude Monet: Paintings in California Collections,” no. 11.

The Art Institute of Chicago, March 15–May 11, 1975. “Paintings by Monet,” no. 118.

Basel, Kunstmuseum Basel, July 20–October 19, 1986. “Claude Monet: Nympheas, Impression–Vision,” no. 30.

Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum, April 10–June 14, 1992; Fukuoka Art Museum, July 1–26, 1992; Osaka Municipal Museum of Art, August 8–September 13, 1992; Yokohama, Sogo Museum of Art, September 23–October 25, 1992. “European Masters from the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco,” no. 63.

Canberra, Australian National Gallery, November 14, 1992–January 31, 1993; Melbourne, National Gallery of Victoria, February 19–May 10, 1993; Auckland City Art Museum, June 5–August 29, 1993. “Rembrandt to Renoir: European Masterpieces from the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco,” no. 63.

San Francisco, Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, June 17– September 17, 2006; Raleigh, North Carolina Museum of Art, October 15, 2006– January 14, 2007; The Cleveland Museum of Art, February 18–May 20, 2007. “Monet in Normandy,” no. 59.

Paris, Galeries nationales, Grand Palais, September 22, 2010–January 24, 2011. “Claude Monet: 1840–1926,” no. 166.

Hartford, CT, Wadsworth Atheneum, February 17–June 12, 2011. “Monet’s Water Lilies: An Artist’s Obsession,” no. 7.

Charlottenlund, DK, Ordrupgaard, August 24–December 4, 2016. “Monet: Beyond Impressionism,” no cat. no.

San Francisco, The Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco (de Young Museum), February 16– May 27, 2019; Fort Worth, Kimbell Art Museum, June 16– September 15, 2019. “Monet: The Late Years,” no. 11.

The Hague, Kunstmuseum Den Haag, October 12, 2019–February 2, 2020. “Monet: The Garden Paintings.”

provenance:
The artist’s studio, Giverny, France [1]
By descent, to his son, Michel Monet (1878-1966), Giverny, France
[Sold to Katia Granoff, Paris, ca. 1955] [2]
Sold to John Huston, Los Angeles and Ireland, 1956
[Possibly sold to O’Hana Gallery, London, 1970] [3]
[Spencer A. Samuels & Co., New York, by 1971] [4]
Sold to Mrs. Enid Annenberg Haupt, New York, 1971
[Consigned to Spencer A. Samuels & Co., New York, 1972]
Sold to the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, 1973

[1] See Wildenstein 1996 IV, p. 843, no. 1788.
[2] Per letter from Marc Larock, director general of Galerie Katia Granoff, 24 September 1991, object file, Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco.
[3] Per Wildenstein 1996 IV, p. 843, no. 1788.
[4] As listed in 10 November 1972 invoice received from Spencer A. Samuels &Co., object file, Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco.
